ledger.note: 1826: Penang, Malacca and Singapore are combined as the Straits Settlements under the East India Company. Infobox: 'Established under East India Co. rule: 1826'; 'Capital: George Town (1826-1832); Singapore (1832-1946)'. Penang came in 1786 ('The first settlement was the Penang territory, in 1786'), Province Wellesley in 1800 ('The first grant was in 1800, followed by another in 1831'), Singapore in 1819 ('a British trading post'), and Malacca 'was ceded to the British in the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824' (signed 17 March 1824, transfer on 1 March 1825). [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: counterpart was british-colonial-empire; the prince-of-wales-island dossier dissolves into this one in 1826 (History of Penang: in 1826 the EIC amalgamated Penang, Singapore and Malacca into the Straits Settlements)]
1832: the capital moves from George Town to Singapore (infobox: 'George Town (1826-1832); Singapore (1832-1946)').
1867: the Straits Settlements become a Crown colony. 'Converted to Crown colony: 1 April 1867' (infobox); until then a 'Division within Bengal Presidency (1826-1867)'.

region.text: the Dindings: Pulau Dinding and the Pangkor islands off the Perak coast, with the mainland strip at Lumut

ledger.note: 1874: the Dindings. The Pangkor Treaty was 'signed between Great Britain and the Sultan of Perak on 20 January 1874' and 'the Pulo Dinding and the islands of Pangkor were ceded to Great Britain'; the Straits Settlements page says the Dindings 'were ceded by Perak to the British government under the Pangkor Treaty of 1874'. The Seberang Perai page adds that the treaty also enlarged Province Wellesley's territory to the Kerian River in the south, inside the Pulau Pinang unit.

region.text: Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands

ledger.note: 1886: the Indian Ocean islands. 'Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands were added in 1886.'

1907: Labuan joins the Straits Settlements. 'By 30 October 1906, the British Government proposed to extend the boundaries of the Straits Settlements to include Labuan'; 'The proposal took effect from 1 January 1907.' Labuan had been a Crown colony since 1848 and run by the British North Borneo Company from 1890 (infobox: UK 1904-1906). The Straits Settlements page adds that it became 'a separate settlement within it in 1912'. [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: counterpart was british-colonial-empire; the colony-of-labuan dossier records the 1 January 1907 loss to this dossier (Crown Colony of Labuan page: incorporation took effect from 1 January 1907)]

region.text: the Dindings: Pulau Dinding and the Pangkor islands off the Perak coast, with the mainland strip at Lumut

ledger.note: 1935: the Dindings go back to Perak. 'It was returned to Perak in February 1935.'
1941: Penang falls to Japan. Japan landed in Kelantan on 8 December 1941; Penang 'fell on 16 December 1941, the first settlement to fall'.
1942: Labuan is occupied by Japan 'from 3 January 1942 until June 1945'.
1942: Malacca falls to Japan on 15 January 1942.
1942: Singapore falls on 15 February 1942, the last settlement to fall.
1945: Labuan is freed in June 1945 (Labuan page: occupied 'from 3 January 1942 until June 1945').

1945: Penang freed. The occupation lasted 'until the end of the war in August 1945'; the infobox gives the 'Formal surrender by Japan to British Military Administration: 12 September 1945' (month 9 used).
1945: Malacca freed (same dating as Penang: end of the war in August, formal surrender 12 September 1945).
1945: Singapore freed (same dating as Penang: end of the war in August, formal surrender 12 September 1945).

1946: Labuan goes to North Borneo. 'Labuan then on 15 July 1946 joined the North Borneo Crown Colony' (Labuan page); the Straits Settlements page dissolves the colony 'with effect from 1 April 1946', so the event sits at the colony's end (month 4) to keep the island inside its life; the Labuan page's 15 July is the date of the transfer.

notes:
Written 2026-10-20 by the se-03-x additions batch: a colony Cliopatria lacks (its settlements sit inside the british-colonial-empire row, 1895 on). Five pages opened (the budget).
Unsettled: (1) Penang 1786, Province Wellesley 1800 and Singapore 1819 precede the life of 1826 (the page's 'established' year), so they appear in the predecessors and in the found event, not as separate gains; the Kedah and Johor dossiers hold their losses (counterpart british-colonial-empire). The Anglo-Dutch Treaty page is silent on Singapore and on a separate Malacca handover date other than the general 1 March 1825. (2) The 1831 northward extension and the 1874 Kerian enlargement of Province Wellesley are below one grid cell; they are described in notes, not drawn. (3) The Seberang Perai page is silent on the 1786 cession and on 1802/1805; the 1859 and 1867/1868 boundary changes are dated differently by that page (1868). (4) Christmas Island: the page says 1886 (some other sources 1900); the page is followed. The Cocos Islands' annexation as a Straits Settlements dependency may be 1886 as well; neither is a state with a dossier. (5) The Dindings circle (20 km at 100.6E 4.22N) is the researcher's reading; gazetteer names Lumut and Pangkor are missing. (6) Successors that need dossiers: Malayan Union (1946-1948) and Colony of Singapore (1946-1963); North Borneo is in this batch (british-north-borneo). (7) The Japanese occupation ends 'in August 1945' (page) or 12 September 1945 (infobox): month 9 is used. (8) Labuan: Brunei ceded it in 1846 (Treaty of Labuan, 18 December 1846, accession 24 December) and it was a Crown colony from 1848; its own dossier (Labuan, 1846-1907 and 1907-1946) is not written. (9) Rulers: none (governors are not listed on the pages opened).
